newsitem.title: USA: Canadian Pacific may oppose Conrail deal.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific may oppose Conrail deal.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd's Delaware & Hudson rail line will oppose the proposed purchase of Conrail Inc if buyers Norfolk Southern Corp and CSX Corp do not address competitive issues.

The line that links Canadian markets to New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania risks losing millions in revenue from the proposed transaction despite a recent haulage rights pact with Norfolk Southern, said Steve Fisk, senior manager of business development for the division that operates D&H.
Canadian Pacifiic said other issues must be resolved for D&H to remain viable in the Northeast.
"Unless those access issues are addressed, we're going to oppose the merger," Fisk told Reuters in an interview after speaking at a meeting of the Transportation Research Forum Thursday.

Norfolk Southern and CSX have proposed buying Conrail for $10.3 billion and dividing the assets of the Northeast freight railroad. Prior to the transaction, D&H partnered with Norfolk Southern and CSX in competing against Conrail.
"Under the breakup of Conrail they will become competitors to the D&H," Fisk said.
"It is not possible for the D&H to compete against these newly enlarged Class 1 railroads without the removal of Conrail-era restrictions on its access into the Northeast markets."

D&H wants the elimination of intermodal restrictions on its trackage rights to New Jersey, the removal of certain freight exclusivity barriers and improved access to ports in Buffalo, Philadelphia, Camden and Baltimore.
It is also seeking a more direct route between Albany and the metropolitan New York/New Jersey market.

Canadian Pacific, which bought D&H in 1991 and has invested $200 million in the line, would file its opposition before the federal Surface Transportation Board, which oversees railroad transactions, Fisk said.

"We've got a $200 million investment and our shareholders have a $200 million investment," Fisk said. "The goal is to get what we need, whether they negotiate it, or whether we do it through the STB."
